name: Halvek Cardamom-Plum Mood Gels
description: Soft translucent gels in deep violet, each containing a micro-dose of serotoninergic plant compounds alongside a warm cardamom-smoked plum flavor. Effects are subtle: a mild smoothing of emotional edges over forty-five minutes.
flavor_profile: Warm spiced cardamom leading into jammy smoked plum, with a faint floral aftertaste from the bioactive compound
cultural_context: Halvek Mood Gels are the working-class alternative to prescription mood management. Many Tier 2 users are deeply loyal, describing them as 'the thing that gets me through the second half of the shift.' They sit in a legal but contested space — corponation lobbyists periodically push to reclassify them as pharmaceuticals, which would price most users out.
story_hooks: A reclassification bill is moving through the city council, and Halvek's street-level distributor network is quietly organizing political resistance — using candy deliveries as cover for coalition meetings.
A Tier 1 user has been eating six to eight Halvek gels a day for two years, far above recommended dosage, and is experiencing a personality change that her family can't explain.

Someone is selling counterfeit Halvek gels with a different compound inside — not dangerous, but not mood-modulating either. The counterfeiter is pocketing the difference while users wonder why they stopped working.
